name: Backward-Planned Work
principle: Work is planned backwards from a written, checkable done-standard, so every step serves a condition that can be seen to be met.
state_description: Before a deep run starts, the goal says what must be true when it ends; the run works toward that condition and reports against it, so the person can tell from the report whether the work reached it.
hints_of_measurement: Compare, on the same deep goals, whether each run starts from a stated done-standard and whether its final report names the evidence for it; a run with no stated standard counts against it.

name: Consistent Account State
principle: What the AI says about the person's own account is true of the account when it says it, every time in a session.
state_description: Asking twice what state the account is in gets the same answer unless something changed, and then the answer says what changed; a change it made is reported once.
hints_of_measurement: State claims match the store at reply time across scripted sessions; no two answers in a session contradict; no change is repeated or re-proposed after it ran.

name: Shared Quest Operations
principle: Quest's operations are implemented once, and each way of reaching them (in the same process as Quest, or over its HTTP API) gives the same results.
state_description: Whether Quest AI runs inside Quest or beside it, the same request changes the account in the same way and returns the same answer; a fix to an operation reaches both without a second edit.
hints_of_measurement: The same operation called through each access point returns the same result and the same typed outcome (applied, held, noop, refused, failed or unknown) on the same account state; no operation exists at one access point only.
